name: Whistle loudly
blurb: The two-finger taxi whistle. Genuinely useful for calling dogs, children and attention across a field, and it is a technique problem rather than a talent.
steps: Make the tongue shape: curl the tip of your tongue back and up so the underside faces forward.
Form a small circle with thumb and middle finger, or use two index fingers, and place the tips just inside your lips against the underside of your tongue, pushing it back.
Seal your lips firmly over your fingers and teeth — the seal does most of the work.
Blow steadily downward across the tongue edge, not hard. Adjust the tongue angle in tiny increments while blowing.
When you get a note, freeze the exact position and repeat it before you lose it.
Practise daily; expect several days of air noise before the first squeak.
tips: Blowing harder never helps. The note comes from the angle, then volume follows.
Wet lips help the seal. A dry mouth makes it nearly impossible.
Nearly everyone can learn this, but it can take a fortnight of daily failure first.
proof: A loud, clear whistle on demand, first attempt, three times running.
